Orsted AS Unveils New Grid-Scale Battery System in Denmark to Boost Renewable Integration

Orsted AS, the Danish electric utilities leader, has launched a new grid-scale battery energy storage system (BESS) aimed at strengthening grid stability and supporting a higher share of renewable energy in Denmark’s power mix. The project, officially inaugurated on Tuesday at a site near Esbjerg, marks Orsted’s first commercial-scale battery installation in its domestic market.

The 25 MW/50 MWh facility is designed to help balance fluctuations in wind and solar generation, responding to Denmark’s ambitious targets for phasing out fossil fuels. “This launch is a significant step towards a more flexible and resilient energy system,” said Søren Mikkelsen, Orsted’s Senior Vice President for Asset Operations, speaking at the opening event. “By integrating large-scale batteries, we are making it easier to match renewable supply with demand and ensuring a more stable grid for Danish consumers and businesses.”

The installation, built in collaboration with the Danish grid operator and supported by local engineering firm Vesthavn Technologies, is expected to provide frequency regulation and reserve capacity services. According to preliminary estimates, the system could reduce curtailment of wind power in western Denmark by up to 7% annually, equivalent to powering nearly 4,000 households.

Industry observers view the launch as a timely response to Denmark’s surging renewable generation. “With wind and solar now accounting for over half of Denmark’s electricity, we need innovative storage solutions to maintain reliability,” said Poul Eriksen, an analyst at the Nordic Energy Institute. “Orsted’s project is a clear example of how utilities can enable a more dynamic and sustainable grid.”

The Danish Energy Association welcomed the move, noting that energy storage is increasingly vital as Denmark aims for a 70% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions by 2030. “Grid-scale batteries like this are essential for realising our climate goals,” said spokesperson Mette Jørgensen. “They help manage variability and reduce the need for backup from fossil plants.”

Orsted AS indicated that lessons learned from the Esbjerg project will inform future storage investments, both in Denmark and in international markets. The company plans to monitor the facility’s performance closely over the next year, with potential to scale up capacity as renewable integration accelerates.
